title: The borrowed view
bodyMd:
In a fictional apartment renovation, a designer proposed enlarging a window to improve daylight. Computer images showed a bright room facing an open garden. During a site visit, the client learned that the neighbouring land had permission for a new building. The proposed window would still admit light, but the future view and shading could differ substantially from the images.

The designer prepared two sets of studies: one using the existing surroundings and one using the permitted development. Neither was presented as a certain prediction of the final scene. The second study nevertheless mattered because it tested a documented possibility that the first images omitted. The client concluded that a persuasive image should state its assumptions, especially when its appeal depends on conditions outside the designer’s control.
